1A.6.note: All 112 operations generated from Smithy model via six per-language generators (Go, TypeScript, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Rust)

1B.2.note: Request/response types generated from OpenAPI schema, not hand-constructed

1B.4.note: Optional fields use pointers (Go), optional (TS/Swift/Kotlin), nilable (Ruby), Option (Rust)

1B.5.note: Timestamps are strings in every language; openapi.json types the 29 *_at fields as plain string with no format: date-time, so ISO 8601 rests on the Smithy ISO8601Timestamp type name alone

1C.1.note: Generated service paths match the spec, but the hand-written magic-link flows in Go, TypeScript, Ruby, Swift and Kotlin post to /sessions-style paths the spec does not have (it has /session.json and /session/magic_link.json); only Rust uses the generated routes

1C.3.note: Service paths are generated in every language, but the hand-written magic-link flows in Go (magic_link.go), TypeScript (auth/magic-link.ts), Ruby (magic_link_flow.rb), Swift (Auth/MagicLinkFlow.swift) and Kotlin (auth/MagicLinkFlow.kt) build their own paths rather than using the generated routes; Rust uses routes::CREATE_SESSION and routes::REDEEM_MAGIC_LINK

2A.6.note: Rust keeps a 10 KB prefix of an error body; Go reads at most 1 MB and drops a larger one; Ruby skips parsing past 1 MB after Faraday buffers it; TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin read the whole error body with no cap

2D.5.note: Go and Rust hold breaker and bulkhead registries per client instance (keyed by Service.Operation within it) and one rate limiter per client, with no global state; TypeScript, Ruby, Swift and Kotlin ship resilience primitives the client does not apply

3A.4.note: OAuth PKCE deferred — Fizzy does not implement OAuth

3A.5.note: OAuth PKCE deferred — Fizzy does not implement OAuth

3A.6.note: Token auto-refresh deferred — Fizzy uses session tokens, not refresh tokens

3C.2.note: Success bodies are capped at 50 MB in Go (while reading) and Ruby (after buffering) and at 10 MiB by default in Rust; TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin have no cap

3C.3.note: Error messages truncated to 500 bytes or characters in all six languages; TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin read the full body before truncating (see 3C.2, 2A.6)

3C.4.note: Hooks receive method, URL, attempt and result, never headers, so they cannot log Authorization or Cookie; Go, TypeScript, Ruby and Rust also export header-redaction helpers, which only Rust uses (Response Debug)

4B.5.note: AGENTS.md rule 3 requires unit and conformance tests for every new operation; the shared fixtures hold 134 cases across 6 runners (Go, TypeScript, Ruby, Swift, Kotlin, Rust) naming 73 of the 112 operations, with paths, status mapping, retry, idempotency and security behaviors covered for the rest by family

4C.4.note: Release re-runs are safe: Go checks for an existing go/ tag and compares the go/ tree; TypeScript and Rust check the registry before publishing (Rust also matches the sha256); Ruby and Kotlin treat an already-published error as success; Swift has no publish step
